t:
Section 313 of the Federal Corrupt Practices Act, 1925 (U. S. C., 1940 edition, title 2, Sec. 251; Supp. V, title 50, App., see. 1509), as amended, is amended to read as follows:

“Sec. 313. It is unlawful for any national bank, or any corporation organized by authority of any law of Congress, to make a contribution or expenditure in connection with any election to any political office, or in connection with any primary election or political convention or caucus held to select candidates for any political office, or for any corporation whatever, or any labor organization to make a contribution or expenditure in connection with any election at which Presidential and Vice Presidential electors or a Senator or Representative in, or a Delegate or Resident Commissioner to Congress are to be voted for, or in connection with any primary election or political convention or caucus held to select candidates for any of the foregoing offices, or for any candidate, political committee, or other person to accept or receive any contribution prohibited by this section. Every corporation or labor organization which makes any contribution or expenditure in violation of this section shall be fined not more than $5,000; and every officer or director of any corporation, or officer of any labor organization, who consents to any contribution or expenditure by the corporation or labor organization, as the case may be, in violation of this section shall be fined not more than $1,000 or imprisoned for not more than one year, or both. For the purposes of this section ‘labor organization’ means any organization of any kind, or any agency or employee representation committee or plan, in which employees participate and which exists for the purpose, in whole or in part, of dealing with employers concerning grievances, labor disputes, wages, rates of pay, hours of employment, or conditions of work.”

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the word "participate" and the references to elections, conventions, and caucuses signal public participation. But "participate" appears only in the definition of a labor organization, and elections are expressly excluded from the definition. The section is a criminal ban on political contributions by banks, corporations, and labor organizations. It sets up no process in which outside parties are consulted on, comment on, or may sue over a federal decision.
fable.s: in which employees participate and which exists for the purpose, in whole or in part, of dealing with employers

qwen_block.w: The section defines a 'labor organization' as an entity in which employees 'participate,' but this refers to internal membership and collective bargaining activities, not participation in federal government decision-making. The text primarily prohibits corporate and labor contributions to political campaigns and establishes penalties for violations, without requiring consultation with or input from outside parties regarding federal decisions.
qwen_block.s: For the purposes of this section ‘labor organization’ means any organization of any kind, or any agency or employee representation committee or plan, in which employees participate and which exists for the purpose, in whole or in part, of dealing with employers concerning grievances, labor disputes, wages, rates of pay, hours of employment, or conditions of work.

opus.w: This section bans contributions and expenditures by corporations and labor organizations in federal elections, and sets criminal penalties for doing so. The word "participate" appears only in the definition of a labor organization, where it describes employees taking part in that organization. It does not describe outsiders taking part in a federal decision. Elections and the like are excluded traps, and no consultation, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue is created.
opus.s: any organization of any kind, or any agency or employee representation committee or plan, in which employees participate and which exists for the purpose, in whole or in part, of dealing with employers
opus.b: The tempting reading is that this is participation because it mentions elections, labor organizations and committees, and the definition of "labor organization" uses the word "participate." That reading fails. The section is a criminal ban on corporate and union campaign contributions. "Participate" only describes employees inside a labor organization. Elections are expressly excluded under the definition, and no federal decision involves outside parties through consultation, hearings, comment or a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: The section prohibits corporate political contributions and defines 'labor organization' for enforcement purposes. The mention of 'participation' is part of a statutory definition of a labor union's internal structure, not a requirement for the federal government to consult with outside parties before making a decision. There is no mechanism for public comment, advisory boards with non-federal members, or consultation with states/tribes regarding federal actions.
qwen_chat.s: For the purposes of this section ‘labor organization’ means any organization of any kind, or any agency or employee representation committee or plan, in which employees participate and which exists for the purpose, in whole or in part, of dealing with employers concerning grievances, labor disputes, wages, rates of pay, hours of employment, or conditions of work.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the definition of "labor organization" includes the phrase "in which employees participate," suggesting participation. However, this is a definitional clause describing the internal structure of a labor union for the purpose of applying penalties, not a requirement for the federal government to consult with outsiders before making a decision. The section itself is a prohibition on corporate political contributions and does not establish any process for public input, advisory committees, or consultation with non-federal entities regarding federal decisions.
